title: Grill — a multi-threaded, non-blocking Agetor core
summary:
Before I plan this: **9 decisions** that set the shape of the change, then a confirm list of defaults I'd bet on (one click each).

The short version of what I found: the busy banner fires because **one thread does everything**, and two things keep it busy for seconds at a time: **(1)** the board's task-list poll re-reading and re-serializing every task every 2 s, and **(2)** the Claude subagent watcher draining whole transcripts with no yield. Real threads help most for the heavy reads that can't be avoided; the biggest win is not doing the work at all.

Start with the two **Blocking** questions: they decide how big this change is.

proven.text: **The stalls are real and frequent.** A 250 ms `/health` prober on your running app saw **54 stalls of 1–10 s in 10 minutes**. A native `sample` during the stalls shows the core's JS thread ~30–40% inside synchronous SQLite reads (cold overflow-page `pread`s), the rest idle.

evidence.label: fleet knowledge entry 18db0f48 (busy banner root cause)

proven.text: **The board poll costs 0.56–1.16 s every 2 s on your installed 1.2.0** (28.8 MB per response). #305 (now on main) cuts it to the ~450 unarchived tasks, but each tick still rebuilds and re-sends every one of them.

evidence.label: the list query reads every column of every row
evidence.code:
const TASKS_SELECT = `
  SELECT tasks.*,
         COALESCE(MAX(runs.status IN ${OPENABLE_STATUSES_SQL}), 0) AS has_openable_run
    FROM tasks
    LEFT JOIN runs ON runs.task_id = tasks.id
`;

proven.text: **Threads work in the packaged runtime.** A spike on the exact Bun the app ships (1.3.13) started a Worker *inside* the app's own Worker, opened the same SQLite file in WAL mode, ran ~30 MB reads while the main thread wrote every 100 ms: **0 lock errors**, and `/health` max latency dropped **3–4×** versus doing the read on the main thread. It also bundles as a separate file, the way `daemon/headless.js` already ships.

evidence.label: launcher already starts our code in a Worker

proven.text: **The subagent watcher's steady-state tick drains every running transcript in one synchronous go** (every 600 ms while anything runs), with no yield and no lag label. The dir-watcher callback does the same on every file append. The persisted 'attach subagent watcher' stall labels are attributed by overlap, so they don't prove the attach itself is the culprit.

evidence.label: steady-state tick: step(Infinity)

proven: **Making every database call async is a ~900-call-site rewrite** across 46 files (tasks.* ~504, runs.* ~215, plus transactions and exit handlers that need synchronous results). A hybrid that moves only the heavy read paths is a handful of routes.

**`updated_at` can't drive an incremental refresh.** ~17 server-managed columns (unread watermarks, PR links, pipeline progress, checkout branch…) and 4 in-memory counts (pending questions, open terminals, running subagents, stall flag) change a task's JSON without bumping it.
**Your packaged core's logs go to `/dev/null`**, so every stall warning the lag monitor prints is lost. Only stalls that overlap a run's label survive, as a status line in that run.

sections.title: How big this change is
sections.intro: These two set the scope. Everything else follows from them.

questions.title: How far should the multi-threading go?
questions.why: Decides whether this is a focused change (a few routes + the watcher) or a rewrite of the whole data layer.
questions.context: SQLite in Bun is synchronous, so whichever thread runs a query is blocked until it returns. The main thread also serves every HTTP request, SSE stream and timer. The heavy reads are a short list: the full task list, a task's event history (replay, pages, first load up to 16 MB), and the subagent transcript parsing.

options.label: Hybrid: worker threads for the heavy work
options.description: A read-only **DB reader worker** (its own SQLite connection) serves the heavy reads: full task-list snapshots, event-history replay and pages. A **transcript worker** reads and parses subagent JSONL off the main thread and hands back parsed lines; the main thread does the small, ordered inserts. Writes and light reads stay on the main connection.
options.consequence: Moves the cold-disk reads and big JSON parsing off the main thread. A few routes and the watcher change; the ~900 synchronous call sites don't. Tests keep an in-process fallback.

options.label: Full DB worker: every query async
options.description: All SQLite access moves to a worker; every `tasks.*` / `runs.*` call becomes `await`.
options.consequence: ~900 call sites in 46 files, every transaction and exit handler redesigned, async ordering risks in SSE sends. Weeks of work and a large regression surface.

options.label: No threads: just stop doing the work
options.description: Incremental task list, cooperative watcher, SQLite cache, logs, all on the one thread.
options.consequence: Smaller change, but a cold-disk read under memory pressure still freezes everything for its duration.

recommendation.reason: It moves exactly the work the samples showed blocking, at a fraction of the risk of a full rewrite, and the spike proved it on your runtime.

questions.title: How should the board and TUI keep their task lists fresh?
questions.why: This is the single biggest recurring cost: today every tick rebuilds and re-sends every visible task.
questions.context: Because `updated_at` misses most changes, any 'only what changed' scheme needs a real change counter. The cleanest source is the database itself: a small new table (`task_revs`: task id → revision) kept current by **SQLite triggers** on `tasks` and `runs`, so no write path can forget to bump it. Deletions leave a tombstone row. The in-memory counts (pending questions, terminals, running subagents, stall flag) are tiny and sent every tick as a sparse map instead.

options.label: Delta poll
options.description: `GET /tasks?since=<rev>` returns only rows whose revision moved (plus removed ids and the small count map). Plain `GET /tasks` stays exactly as today for older clients. Board keeps its 2 s tick; TUI its 1.5 s.
options.consequence: An idle board costs one indexed lookup per tick instead of ~450 rows. One additive migration (a table + triggers).

options.label: Delta poll + push
options.description: Same delta, plus a tiny `tasks-changed {rev}` event on the existing global SSE stream so the board fetches the delta the moment something changes, and the timer stretches to a 15 s safety net.
options.consequence: Board updates feel instant and idle polling nearly disappears. No new connection (reuses the existing stream). A bit more client logic and one more event type.

options.label: Whole-list ETag / 304
options.description: The server still builds the list, but returns 304 when nothing changed.
options.consequence: Saves network and webview parsing only; the core still does the heavy read every tick.

recommendation.reason: Push makes changes show up immediately and lets the poll become a safety net; the delta protocol underneath keeps it correct if an event is missed.

questions.title: Which changes to the Claude subagent watcher?
questions.why: The watcher is the second source of multi-second stalls on your machine.
questions.context: Its steady-state tick (`cycle()` → `step(Infinity)`, `src/bun/claude-subagents.ts:4192`) and the fs.watch callback (`:4034`) drain every running transcript synchronously. Each 256 KB chunk does a JSON.parse per line plus an autocommit INSERT and a broadcast per line.

options.label: Deadline-bound every pass
options.description: Tick and dir-watcher passes run as cooperative jobs (20 ms slices with a yield), resuming next tick instead of draining everything at once.

options.label: Read + parse transcripts in the transcript worker
options.description: File reads and JSON.parse happen off the main thread; the main thread receives ready lines.

options.label: Batch inserts per chunk
options.description: One transaction per chunk instead of one autocommit per line; live sends still go out in id order right after the commit.

options.label: Fix the lag label
options.description: The 'attach subagent watcher' label covers only the attach work itself, so stall reports stop blaming it for unrelated stalls.

recommendation.reason: Each fixes a different piece; together they take the watcher off the critical path.

questions.title: Which other main-thread blockers should this change also fix?
questions.why: Smaller, rarer stalls the investigation found. Leaving one out means it stays.

options.label: Boot: login-shell PATH probe
options.description: `login-path.ts` runs `$SHELL -ilc` synchronously at boot (up to 2 s). Make it async.

options.label: Request-path file scans
options.description: Claude session scan, account usage (recursive read with an uncapped slice), worktrees listing: switch to async fs and cap reads.

options.label: git provider `ssh -G` probe
options.description: A synchronous spawn per call; make it async and cached.

options.label: Recursive rmSync on delete / clone cleanup

recommendation.reason: They're small, contained, and each one can freeze the whole app for its duration.

questions.title: What's the longest the main thread may be blocked by any single unit of work?
questions.why: Becomes the acceptance bar the tests and the benchmark enforce.
questions.context: The previous responsiveness work set a 100 ms bar and measured 43–45 ms worst case for session restore.

recommendation.reason: Matches the bar the codebase already tests against, and is well under what a person notices as a freeze.

questions.title: Target /health p95 latency while heavy work runs (opening a long transcript, a big subagent run, the board polling)?
questions.why: The busy banner keys off /health; this is the number that says the banner is gone.

recommendation.reason: Two missed 1.5 s probes trigger the banner; 100 ms p95 leaves a wide margin.

questions.title: How should it ship?
questions.why: This touches the DB layer, the server, the watcher, the webview and the CLI.

options.label: One PR, one commit per wave
options.description: What you asked for: one PR later, reviewable wave by wave.

options.label: A stack of PRs
options.description: e.g. logs + cache → delta task list → workers → watcher; each wired and green on its own.

recommendation.reason: You asked for one PR; wave commits keep it reviewable.

questions.title: SQLite memory settings
questions.context: Today it's the 2 MB default against a 4.6 GB database, so every poll re-reads pages. mmap lets hot pages be served without a read syscall.

recommendation.value: `cache_size` 64 MB and `mmap_size` 256 MB on the main connection; the reader worker gets the same.
recommendation.reason: Small next to the webview's footprint, and it keeps the hot tables in memory.

recommendation.value: `~/.agetor/logs/core.log`, mode 0600, rotated at 5 MB × 3 files, written by a buffered async writer (never a sync write per line), secrets redacted. Every stall ≥ 1 s is logged, with or without a task label.
recommendation.reason: Today's warnings vanish into /dev/null; this makes the next slowdown diagnosable.

questions.title: Compact database (VACUUM)
questions.context: A VACUUM on another thread still takes an exclusive lock, so the main thread's writes would have to wait on it, which is a block of its own.

recommendation.value: Leave it as it is: manual, refused while a run is active. Out of scope.
recommendation.reason: Moving it doesn't remove the lock; out of scope.

recommendation.value: Keep it exactly as it is (observational; 3 s pending plus two missed /health probes).
recommendation.reason: It's the right alarm; the fix is to stop tripping it.

recommendation.value: Add `scripts/measure-core-responsiveness.ts`: a headless core on a `.backup` copy of a real-sized DB in `~/.agetor-dev`, driving the board poll, a transcript replay and a subagent run, reporting /health p50/p95/max and the longest main-thread block, before and after. Never touches ~/.agetor.
recommendation.reason: Turns 'feels faster' into numbers, and never touches your real ~/.agetor.

recommendation.value: Extend the busy-banner and board specs: a heavy load (big transcript replay + many tasks) runs while the test asserts the board keeps updating and the banner never appears; plus a delta/push spec for the board.
recommendation.reason: The bug is user-visible; only the assembled app proves it's gone.

questions.title: Anything that has to be true before you'd call this done?
questions.placeholder: e.g. no busy banner during a day of normal use
